registers.name_in_paper: the Danish Vaccination Register (Det danske vaccinationsregister, DDV)
registers.role: outcomes: date and type of all vaccinations administered, identified via the national vaccination codes
covariate used in a descriptive balance table and in an adjusted sensitivity logistic regression
variables_mentioned: municipality type (Capital, Commuter, Metropolitan, Provincial, Rural Municipalities)

linkages: Children identified in the Danish Civil Registration Register and linked to their vaccination records in the DDV through unique national identification numbers
Scheduled vaccination dates computed per child from date of birth (and the date of the relevant previous vaccination) using the same algorithm as the national vaccination schedule

sample.universe: All children born in January 2018 or in January 2022 and registered in the Danish Civil Registration Register (source population n = 10,490)
selection_rules: All children born in January 2018 (control cohort) and January 2022 (intervention cohort) selected: source population n = 10,490
Exclude children who did not live in Denmark during the entire study period (16.5 months): n = 695 excluded, leaving a study population of n = 9,795 (control 4,976; intervention 4,819)
For each vaccination, exclude children vaccinated more than two weeks before the scheduled vaccination date (DTaP-IPV/Hib1: 41 control, 16 intervention; MMR1: 670 control, 58 intervention)
DTaP-IPV/Hib1 analysis: control n = 4,935; intervention n = 4,803. MMR1 analysis: control n = 4,306; intervention n = 4,761
DTaP-IPV/Hib2 analysis restricted to children vaccinated with DTaP-IPV/Hib1 inside its follow-up window (excluded: 560 control, 257 intervention): control n = 4,375; intervention n = 4,546

DTaP-IPV/Hib3 analysis restricted to the children in the DTaP-IPV/Hib2 analysis vaccinated with DTaP-IPV/Hib2 inside its follow-up window (excluded: 572 control, 328 intervention): control n = 3,803; intervention n = 4,218
sample.period: Children born January 2018 followed to 16.5 months (into 2019) and children born January 2022 followed to 16.5 months (into 2023)
sample.n_observations: 9,795 children (4,976 control; 4,819 intervention); analysis samples differ by vaccination

construction_notes: Scheduled vaccination dates were manually calculated with the same algorithm used to assign the vaccination schedule at birth, based on the child's date of birth and/or the date of the relevant previous vaccination
Follow-up for each vaccination runs from two weeks before the scheduled vaccination date (the day the invitation letter is sent under the proactive system) to six weeks after it: 8 weeks in total
If the start-of-follow-up date fell on a Sunday it was moved to the following Monday, because invitation and reminder letters are not sent on Sundays
Vaccination coverage = vaccinated children divided by the total number of children included in that analysis per cohort

A child counts as entirely unvaccinated if it has no vaccination registered by the end of the study period (16.5 months) or has a vaccination registered that is not the one of interest for the respective analysis

The DTaP-IPV/Hib1 and MMR1 analyses use the whole study population (including entirely unvaccinated children); the DTaP-IPV/Hib2 and DTaP-IPV/Hib3 analyses use selective sub-cohorts conditioned on receipt of the previous dose

Cohorts were chosen so that the control cohort's vaccinations were completed before the reminder system was implemented (August 2019) and so that the intervention cohort's vaccinations fall after all COVID-19 restrictions were lifted (February 2022) and outside Christmas holidays
All analyses conducted in R Statistical Software v. 4.4.0

links.pointer_quote: The vaccination coverage at six weeks after scheduled vaccination was higher for children in the intervention cohort for all vaccinations, except the second diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis-polio-Hib vaccine (DTaP-IPV/Hib2) given at 5 months.

Children in the intervention group were significantly more likely to have been vaccinated at six weeks after scheduled vaccination for all vaccinations except DTaP-IPV/Hib2, compared to the control group.

claims.statement: Children covered by the proactive reminder system (born January 2022) were significantly more likely to be vaccinated with DTaP-IPV/Hib1 at six weeks after the scheduled vaccination date than children born January 2018.

treatment.label: Proactive childhood vaccination reminder system (intervention cohort, born January 2022) versus no proactive reminder system (control cohort, born January 2018)

register_source.value: Danish Civil Registration Register (date of birth, which defines cohort membership); the paper names no register variable

definition.value: Binary birth-cohort indicator. Children born in January 2022 were vaccinated under the proactive reminder system that Denmark implemented in August 2019: parents receive an electronic invitation letter two weeks before each scheduled vaccination and an electronic reminder letter four weeks after the scheduled vaccination date if no vaccination has been recorded in the Danish Vaccination Register (DDV). Children born in January 2018 were vaccinated before the system existed (control).

timing.value: Cohort membership fixed at birth; the invitation letter is sent 14 days before each scheduled vaccination date (which is also the start of follow-up) and the reminder letter four weeks after the scheduled date, i.e. inside the 8-week follow-up window of each vaccination

outcome.label: Vaccinated with DTaP-IPV/Hib1 at six weeks after the scheduled vaccination date

register_source.value: Danish Vaccination Register (Det danske vaccinationsregister, DDV): date and type of vaccination, identified through the national vaccination codes

definition.value: Binary indicator of whether the child had received DTaP-IPV/Hib1 (first tetanus, diphtheria, acellular pertussis, polio, Haemophilus influenzae type b vaccination, scheduled at 3 months) by six weeks after the scheduled vaccination date; the follow-up window runs from two weeks before the scheduled date to six weeks after it (8 weeks in total). Coverage is the proportion of vaccinated children divided by the total number of children included in that analysis per cohort.

timing.value: Measured at six weeks after the scheduled vaccination date for that dose (scheduled at 3, 5, 12 and 15 months of age respectively)

units.value: odds ratio for being vaccinated at six weeks, intervention cohort versus control cohort

magnitude.interpretation: Children in the intervention cohort were 25 % more likely to be vaccinated with the DTaP-IPV/Hib1 vaccination (OR: 1.25, 95 % CI 1.06–1.48); the coverage at six weeks was 1.3 percentage points higher (control: 93.3 % vs intervention: 94.6 %).
